What this answers

If we move price by 1%, how much does volume move, and is a price cut revenue-positive?

How to read it

Below -1 means volume responds more than price, so a cut can grow revenue. Between -1 and 0 volume barely reacts. Positive values usually mean import cost is driving both price and volume, not pricing power. R-squared shows how much of the movement price explains; Level beta is the cross-check.

Source

First-difference regression of monthly ln(volume) on ln(realized price) per SKU, needing 8 or more month-to-month pairs and a fit of R² 0.10+ to be ranked.

Measurable SKUs
18+ months, real price variation
Elastic (< −1)
volume responds more than price
Inelastic (−1…0)
volume sticky to price
Anomalous (> 0)
cost pass-through / supply driven

How to read it. β is the % change in volume per 1% change in price, estimated from month-to-month movements so the shared cost trend cancels out. −2.0 means a 10% price cut moves volume 20%; revenue rises only when |β| > 1. Click a bar or a row to see the SKU’s own data and a plain-language read. Commodity codes often print positive values because import cost drives both price and volume.

What this answers

When our price moved, did volume follow because of us — or because the whole market moved? This compares our realized price with the same pack sold by competitor brands.

How to read it

Comparison is like-for-like: same product form and same pack size (e.g. Chinigura 1kg vs Chinigura 1kg), not a category average. “Premium vs MRP/DP” is our realized price against the market average. The verdict says whether we led the market, followed it, or moved against it.

Source

oms.tblCompetitorPriceHeader / Row / Product — market price surveys by brand and pack. Coverage is limited: May–Dec 2024 only, and bulk 50 KG rows carry no MRP in the ERP.

What this answers

What price has AEL actually declared for each SKU — distributor price, trade price and MRP — and how far is the realized price from it?

How to read it

DP is the Distributor channel price (what the distributor pays). TP is the Dealer channel price (what the retailer pays). MRP is the consumer price. Gap to TP shows whether the SKU is trading above or below its declared trade price — a large negative gap means the grid is stale or discounts are deep.

Source

itm.tblPriceSetup (channels 70 Dealer and 71 Distributor, monthly since Jul-2023) and rtm.tblRetailPrice / tblRetailPriceLog (which also carries MRP). Blank means the ERP holds no declared price for that SKU.

What this answers

For each material SKU and category: what does the evidence say we should do about price — hold it, restore it, cut it, or stop using price as the lever?

How to read it

Every row shows the evidence that produced the call: revenue in view, price change, volume change, elasticity and the gap to declared TP. Decision is the finding, Direction is the pricing stance, Action is the next concrete step. Rows follow the current date / channel / category filters.

Source

All from the same order rows and declared price grid as the other tabs. Thresholds are stated in the Decision column (|β| > 1, ±2% price move, 5% gap to TP) so the rule can be audited.

SKUCategoryRevenuePrice ΔVolume ΔβR²vs TPDecisionDirectionAction
Scope of the call. These are pricing decisions, not commercial judgement: the rules only look at realized price, volume, elasticity and the declared grid. They do not know about COGS (not in this extract), stock cover, or competitor stock — so a “price-led growth” call must be checked against margin before it is executed.

Method

  • Realized price = net value ÷ quantity, per selling unit as booked.
  • Month-on-month price compares to the previous month with sales for that SKU.
  • Elasticity = slope of Δln(volume) on Δln(realized price) between consecutive months (first-difference estimator), which strips out the shared cost/season trend. Needs 15+ monthly differences and |β|≤8 to be reported; the level (log-log) estimate is shown alongside.
  • Declared price for a SKU-month resolves in this order: channel price grid (DP = channel 71, TP = channel 70) → retail price log (DP/TP/MRP) → blank. MRP comes only from the retail table.
  • Volume is in each SKU's own selling unit — never add volumes across SKUs.
  • Where realized price ÷ MRP is outside 0.35–1.6 the booked unit does not reconcile to the declared pack; flagged “unit ?”.
